### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class), saveMetaItem (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_

- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via saveMetaItem (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via saveMetaItem (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via saveMetaItem (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 022c6e799e88ae192e124c80e1cc343bda54d7bf` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b4e7f2f556e23ed10da396b69dc72f0afb83fb71` — the merge of head `c8e2d674a861f6e74707e5424c2b4524f635d7fd` into base `022c6e799e88ae192e124c80e1cc343bda54d7bf`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b4e7f2f556e23ed10da396b69dc72f0afb83fb71 && git checkout b4e7f2f556e23ed10da396b69dc72f0afb83fb71
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 022c6e799e88ae192e124c80e1cc343bda54d7bf c8e2d674a861f6e74707e5424c2b4524f635d7fd && git checkout -B drift-repro 022c6e799e88ae192e124c80e1cc343bda54d7bf && git merge --no-ff c8e2d674a861f6e74707e5424c2b4524f635d7fd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 022c6e799e88ae192e124c80e1cc343bda54d7bf
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 022c6e799e88ae192e124c80e1cc343bda54d7bf` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c8e2d674a861f6e74707e5424c2b4524f635d7fd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.save-flow-canonicalization.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-flow-save-retired-spelling.test.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts (`headAt`, `rowToItem`/`storedRowBody`), packages/spec/src/conversions/apply.ts (`applyConversions`, `applyConversionsToFlow`), packages/spec/src/conversions/walk.ts (`mapFlowNodes`, `mapNodeTree`, `renameKey`), packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts (the twelve retired flow entries, `flow-node-http-callout-rename`, `flow-decision-mode-inclusive-explicit`), packages/spec/src/conversions/types.ts (`ConversionNotice`, `retiredFromLoadPath`), packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (`CONVERSIONS_NOT_REPLAYED_AT_REHYDRATION`, `canonicalizeStoredFlow`, `canonicalizeFlow`), objectui at `origin/main` `a2f38dd`, HEAD `63d00da` and the pin `daeb77fc84`: packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx (the flow designer: its load, `doSave`, autosave, enable switch and package publish), packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/useDraftAutoSave.ts, packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/DraftConflictDialog.tsx (`DraftVersionGuard`), packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ResourceEditPage.tsx (the other editor that holds a flow), packages/data-objectstack/src/draft-envelope.ts (`extractDraftBody`), apps/console/src/components/StudioRoute.tsx and packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx (which editor each route mounts); PR #23954's diff to registry.ts, engine.ts and stored.ts. The .changeset file is the prose face, read under ②.

Inputs: card #23903 (body and all six comments, the director delta 6215813374, the ruling 6216220018, triage's unlock 6217547376, the claim 6218148190, the dev report 6219774643), the prior ruling 6212082860 on #23775, PR #23986's body, file list and net diff against `main` at the head (merge base `0b6956490`), the head's check-runs read seven times, open PR #23954.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff changes one thing a caller can observe: the accept set of the flow save door (`saveMetaItem`, so `PUT /api/v1/meta/flow/:name`, the runtime flow-definition door and every protocol caller) for a save over a STORED row. No export, type or schema moves: `flowSaveReplaysRetired` stays private, the one new import (`ALL_CONVERSIONS`) is already a public export of `@objectstack/spec` (`packages/spec/src/index.ts:231`), `packages/rest` gains a test only. Each accept-set change, read against ruling 6216220018 items 2 to 5 and 6212082860 where B′ inherits from B:

1. **A publish-mode re-save over a stored row whose body fires a retired entry at a site the stored row does not: refused 422 `INVALID_METADATA`, located, the `os validate` text, nothing stored.** Right. Item 2's first clause verbatim; item 4's first pin. The mechanism is the letter's: `flowSaveReplaysRetired` answers `false`, the engine's `canonicalizeStoredFlow` is asked `{ includeRetired: false }` (`protocol.ts:23120`) and the no-engine fallback verdict runs the same option (`:23178`), so the parse refuses on both hosts (#21982 parity kept). Pinned on both hosts in the protocol file and on the real stack at the REST door; the option itself is pinned on the engine stub.

2. **The site identity makes item 4's pin hold when the stored row already carries the SAME spelling on another node.** Right, and this is the load-bearing part. A hit is `conversionId|from|site`, the site being the notice's `path` with every array element that carries a string `id` written `[#id]` (`protocol.ts:6654-6681`, `siteOf` and `retiredHits`). Read in the cited code: every notice the chain can fire carries `conversionId`, `from`, `path` (`apply.ts:189-204`); `applyConversionsToFlow` wraps the body as `{ flows: [flow] }` and never throws (`apply.ts:244`); `mapFlowNodes` writes node paths `flows[i].nodes[j]` and region paths `...config.body.nodes[k]` / `...config.branches[i].nodes[k]` (`walk.ts:179`, `mapNodeTree`); the twelve retired flow entries all emit a KEY name as `from` (`filters`, `config.duration`, `retryDelayMs`, `outputSchema`, `fallbackNodeId`, `config.actionType`, `waitEventConfig.timeoutMs`, …), so a changed VALUE on a carried key is not a new hit, only a new spelling or a new site is. Ids are resolved on the converted body, which no entry reorders. So a node added with `config.filters` beside a stored `config.filters` is `[#n2]` against a carried `[#n1]`: a new hit, refused at `nodes.1.config.filters` naming `filter` (pinned, both hosts; the REST pin does it with `config.duration`, issues `nodes.1.config.duration` and `nodes.2.config.duration`, the second naming `waitEventConfig.timerDuration`). A canonical node inserted in front keeps `[#n1]` carried (pinned). An entry-only or raw-index identity fails exactly these pins (the dev's ablation legs 2 and 3; consistent with the code). Three consequences of an id-keyed site, all inside the letter and all loud: a node whose `id` is renamed is a new site (the dev's acceptance note); a node moved ACROSS regions (top level into a `loop` body) is a new site, so the docblock's "moving a node never turns a carried hit into a new one" is true only within one array; a `parallel` branch carries `name`, not `id` (`control-flow.zod.ts:157`, `:245`), so a branch inserted ahead of one whose nodes carry a retired spelling shifts their site to `[1]` and the re-save is refused as new. None breaks a ruling pin; the refusal names the keys; noted for the approval, not a defect.

3. **Both hosts reach one predicate answer.** Right. The predicate scans request and stored row with the spec's pass, `includeRetired: true` minus `FLOW_FALLBACK_VERDICT_NOT_REPLAYED` (`protocol.ts:3278`, `['flow-decision-mode-inclusive-explicit']`), which equals the engine's `CONVERSIONS_NOT_REPLAYED_AT_REHYDRATION` (`engine.ts:2252`); "retired" is `retiredFromLoadPath` on `ALL_CONVERSIONS`. The engine is never asked for the comparison, so a canonicalizer throw cannot hide a hit. At this base the only live flow entry is `flow-node-http-callout-rename` (`registry.ts:68`, no `retiredFromLoadPath`), whose conflict guard is the one place the engine pass and the spec pass could differ, and it is outside the retired set, so no host split today. The stored body compared is `headAt(...).head.body`, which is `storedRowBody(row)` verbatim (`sys-metadata-repository.ts:776`, `rowToItem`), the row the ruling names.

4. **A re-save whose retired hits the stored row all carries keeps the full chain; the served legacy body re-saves and is healed (engine host) or stored as written (no engine).** Right. Item 2's second clause, item 4's second pin, 6212082860 item 2. Pinned on both hosts and at the REST door (`GET` then `PUT` of the served item: 200).

5. **A new flow with a retired spelling: refused, unchanged from B.** Right. Item 4's third pin; #23902's pins stay green and are untouched by the diff (the `else if (state !== 'draft') return false` leg).

6. **Server-stated writes (`source` set, `package-duplicate`, `package-unmanaged-import`) answer before any read and keep the full chain.** Right. Item 2 verbatim; the two lines are unchanged.

7. **The read path and the engine's rehydration are untouched; C is not taken.** Right. Item 3; `convertStoredItem` still skips `flow` (`protocol.ts:6464`), `engine.ts` is not in the diff.

8. **The whole body is judged in the authoring posture on an introduced hit, so the 422 also lists the carried legacy sites.** Within item 2's letter ("judged with `includeRetired: false`"). A consequence the changeset states, with the fix (correct the added site; the chain then heals the rest). Not a deviation.

9. **DEVIATION from the one-row letter, escalated: for a DRAFT save with a draft row, the ACTIVE row is read as a second carrier (`protocol.ts:6691-6701`).** The letter names one row: 6212082860 item 1 "the lookup the door already makes for its baseline … draft or publish mode does not change it", #23902's ADR note "the row the save overwrites, or for a draft with none yet the active row it overlays", and B′ item 2 "the stored row's body". #23902 read the active row only when no draft row exists; this diff reads it also when the draft row carries none of a request's hits. The premise given for it, that Studio's flow designer keeps its buffer after a draft save so on an engine host its second autosave of a legacy flow would be refused, is **measured true in the designer**: `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx`, the Automations pillar of `/studio/:packageId/automations` (mounted by `apps/console/src/components/StudioRoute.tsx:262`), identical in shape at objectui `origin/main` `a2f38dd`, HEAD `63d00da` and the pin `daeb77fc84`; lines at `a2f38dd`:
   - the load seeds the buffer with the served draft, or with the published row (`client.layered(...).effective`) when no draft row exists (L7062-L7073); `extractDraftBody` strips the read decorations and nothing else (`packages/data-objectstack/src/draft-envelope.ts:59`), and flows are served verbatim, so a legacy flow's buffer holds the legacy spellings;
   - `doSave` (L7105-L7123) sends that buffer `{ mode: 'draft' }` through `saveFlowDraft`, bound at L6836-L6840 from `useDraftSaveGuard` (`DraftVersionGuard`, `DraftConflictDialog.tsx:208-318`, holds a version pin per item and passes the item through); on success it does `setHasDraft(true)` and `setAutoDirty(false)` and nothing else: no draft re-read, no `setDraft`, no reload; only the conflict outcome `'reloaded'` replaces the buffer (L7112, `reloadFlowDraft` L6835). The enable switch saves the same buffer (L7175);
   - `useDraftAutoSave` (L7133-L7141; `useDraftAutoSave.ts:90-164`) re-sends the buffer 1.5 s after each later edit.
   So on an engine host the designer's first autosave of a legacy flow has no draft row, the active row carries the spellings, the full chain runs and the draft row is stored healed; the buffer keeps the legacy spellings; the next edit's autosave re-sends them over the healed draft row while the active row still carries them. Judged against the draft row alone, that save is refused with the carried sites listed, and 6212082860 item 2's "a legacy row stays editable in Studio" is false under B′ from the designer's second autosave on. The union reading is the one that keeps it true: the active row the draft overlays is the row the author was served, so a spelling it carries is inherited, not authored, which is the line the ruling draws. It is bounded on the far side by the designer's own publish: `doPublish` (the package-level `publish-drafts`, or `publishDraft` per flow in the package-less scope) bumps `publishNonce` (L1353, L1435), the flow load re-runs on it (L7094) and re-seeds the buffer from the now-healed published row, so no post-publish autosave carries a legacy spelling. Beyond the designer the reading decides one thing: a non-Studio draft-mode client (REST, or an MCP write tool if one is ever registered) that re-sends a stale legacy body over a healed draft row while the active row still carries the spelling is healed rather than refused; the same client in publish mode is refused (③ flag 1). The other editor that can hold a flow, `metadata-admin/ResourceEditPage.tsx` (`/metadata/flow/:name`, `AppContent.tsx:1036` and `:1134`, with `FlowPreview` as its canvas), re-reads the draft after every save and replaces its buffer (L1686, L1698, L1703, L1706), so it never needs the carrier and is evidence for neither side. The deviation is not the ruling's own premise falsified: its premise, that an uncarried hit is authored input, holds for the node an author adds; what is measured is a gap between B's promise and B′'s one-row letter on the designer's second autosave, which the dev closed by reading the baseline as the pair of rows. That is the maintainer's call, requested in the PR's approval (③ flag 2). Its effect on the accept set is bounded: in that one case it keeps the ruled B's answer (accepted, healed) where the one-row letter refuses; it is never wider than `main` today; the add-a-node refusal still holds on drafts over a stored draft row (pinned, both hosts and REST). The pin "Studio's draft autosaves of a legacy flow keep saving after the first one healed the draft row … and an added node is still refused" models the designer's measured loop; the ADR note's parenthetical "(for a draft, the active row it overlays as well as its own)" records the reading. Both stand if the maintainer confirms it; both change if the maintainer takes the one-row letter.

10. **After PR #23954 (F5-http) lands, the predicate and the pins stay correct.** Read in its diff: `flow-node-http-callout-rename` gains `retiredFromLoadPath: true, retiredAfter: '17.7.0'`, loses the conflict guard and emits `{ from: type, to: canonical, path: `${path}.type` }` unchanged in shape; `apply.ts`, `types.ts`, `FLOW_FALLBACK_VERDICT_NOT_REPLAYED` and `CONVERSIONS_NOT_REPLAYED_AT_REHYDRATION` are not touched; `stored.ts` changes a docblock only and `protocol.ts` still skips `flow` on read. So the three names enter this predicate's retired set by `retiredFromLoadPath` with no edit here; an added `http_request` node is a new site `[#id].type`, judged `includeRetired: false`, and meets #23954's parse refusal at `nodes.N.type` naming `http`; a carried one still renames to `http` under the full chain. With the guard gone, the engine pass and the spec pass agree on every host for that entry too. The pins use `delete_record` `config.filters` and `wait` loose `config.duration`, which #23954 does not move. #23954's own "known gap: the metadata save door" paragraph and its changeset sentence become stale once this lands; that is #23954's seat's edit, not this PR's.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23903-flow-save-reintroduced-retired.md`: `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': minor`, title `feat(metadata-protocol)!:`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, a BREAKING paragraph whose first sentence names the re-save case (ruling item 5), the FROM → TO migration for every spelling the door now refuses, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (already-registered …)` naming twelve D2 ids. Matches what the diff publishes: a narrowing of a published door's accept set is BREAKING under AGENTS.md's grammar ("`(narrowing)` is BREAKING"), `yes` takes at least `minor`, and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` keeps every breaking change at `minor` in the launch window, so `minor` is the repo's breaking level. The twelve ids are exactly the retired flow-surface entries the door can fire (`registry.ts` `surface: 'flow…'` rows minus `flow-decision-mode-inclusive-explicit`, which the door excludes by id, and minus `flow-node-http-callout-rename`, live at this base; its retirement is #23954's registration). `@objectstack/rest` publishes nothing from this diff (a test file), so no second changeset is owed. The PR body's `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` matches the changeset and ruling item 5; `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` concluded `success` on the head. The dev's out-of-scope note that `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` (L11799, L12021) prints "a card that only NARROWS one is `Clause-②: no`" is prose drift against AGENTS.md's grammar and the ruling; the ruling governs and this PR follows it as #23902 did.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and both `open_questions` entries:

1. **`open_questions[0]` — a publish-mode client re-sending its stale legacy body after a healing save is refused on an engine host and accepted on a host with no automation service. Within the ruling's letter; answerable: keep (the dev's A).** Item 2 compares the request with "the stored row's body". The two hosts store different rows by two standing records, the 2026-08-02 save-seam addendum (#4542: an engine host persists `storable`) and #21982 (a no-engine host stores the body as written), so one predicate reads two rows and answers twice. The divergence is in what is stored, not in this predicate; B would add a second notion of "carried" the ruling does not name and would let a stale legacy spelling pass silently; C is a change to #21982's deliberate design, a separate card. The approval sees it as a consequence of the letter, not a question. Studio does not meet it: the designer never sends a publish-mode save; it promotes drafts by package (`StudioDesignSurface.tsx` L1308-L1446) and re-seeds its buffer from the published row on `publishNonce` (L7094).

2. **`open_questions[1]` — the draft baseline includes the active row when a draft row exists. An interpretation the maintainer must confirm; escalated in the PR's approval, with its premise standing.** The letter names one row (① item 9). The premise the PR puts to the maintainer is measured true for Studio's flow designer at objectui `a2f38dd`, `63d00da` and the pin `daeb77fc84` (`StudioDesignSurface.tsx` L7062-L7073, L7105-L7123, L7133-L7141, L7175). The seat tells the maintainer three things in 「席位意见」: (a) what is being confirmed: for a draft save, 「原行」 is the draft row AND the published row it overlays, read as a pair, where the ruling's text names one row; (b) why: without the pair, on a host with an automation service the designer's second autosave of a legacy flow is refused with spellings the author never wrote, because its first autosave healed the draft row and the designer keeps its buffer until a conflict reload or a publish, so B′'s one-row letter breaks 6212082860 item 2 (「a legacy row stays editable in Studio」) from the second autosave on; taking the one-row letter instead would require an objectui change first (the designer re-reading the draft after each save, as `ResourceEditPage.tsx` L1686-L1706 already does) before this PR could land without that breakage on engine hosts; (c) what the pair decides beyond Studio: a non-Studio draft-mode client re-sending a stale legacy body over a healed draft row, while the published row still carries the spelling, is healed rather than refused, whereas the same client in publish mode is refused (flag 1); an added node is refused in every case. If the maintainer confirms, the ADR note's parenthetical and the pin named after Studio stand as written. If the maintainer takes the one-row letter, the diff changes: the active-row read drops once a draft row exists (`protocol.ts:6691-6701`, the `if (target.head)` branch returns `false` when `uncarried` remains), the ADR note's parenthetical goes, the Studio pin is inverted or removed, an objectui card for the designer's post-save re-read is filed first, and a new head gets a new record.

3. **Dev deviation — one import line outside the named symbols (`ALL_CONVERSIONS` from `@objectstack/spec`).** Answered: inside the claimed surface (`protocol.ts`), a public export, no new package dependency; `engine.ts` untouched as the claim required.

4. **Dev acceptance note — the refusal lists the carried sites beside the introduced one.** Answered: the letter (① item 8); the changeset tells the client the one-site fix.

5. **Dev acceptance note — a node whose `id` is renamed while keeping a retired spelling is refused as new.** Answered: the letter (the site is the id); add to the same family, for the approval's awareness, the cross-region move and the id-less `parallel` branch (① item 2). Not a ruling question; a follow-up card only if a measured client meets it.

6. **Dev acceptance note — no MCP metadata-write tool in this repository, no MCP pin constructible.** Answered: #23902's reading stands; ruling item 4's "the same through the REST door" is pinned on the real stack.

7. **Dev out-of-scope — `dispatch-gates.mjs` prose says a narrowing-only card is `Clause-②: no`.** Noted under ②; not this PR's.

8. **Check-runs on the head.** Read seven times (last at the writing of this record): 32 `success`, 6 `skipped`, 0 failed; still `in_progress`: `Test Core (3/6)`. `Test Core (1/6)`, `(2/6)`, `(4/6)`, `(5/6)`, `(6/6)`, `Build Core`, every `Type Check` lane (`workspace`, `source gates`, `consumer gates`, `debt ledger`), every `Lint` lane, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check PR Size`, the claim and single-writer guards have concluded `success`. The verdict below is on what was judged; the one Test Core shard is named here as not yet concluded, and the PR lands on nothing until it does.

9. **Tier H.** The ADR-0087 line is a governed path; the approval is the maintainer's. Item 9 of ① is the one thing that approval decides beyond the ruling's letter.
